title: The Interplay of GPER1 with 17beta-Aminoestrogens in the Regulation of the Proliferation of Cervical and Breast Cancer Cells: A Pharmacological Approach.
authors: Segovia-Mendoza, Mariana; Mirzaei, Elahe; Prado-Garcia, Heriberto; Miranda, Luis D; Figueroa, Alejandra; Lemini, Cristina
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
one_liner_zh: 该文研究GPER1受体与17beta-氨基雌激素的分子对接及细胞增殖效应，属于蛋白-小分子配体互作，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The G-protein-coupled receptor for estrogen (GPER1) is a transmembrane receptor involved in the progression and development of various neoplasms whose ligand is estradiol (E2). 17beta-aminoestrogens (17beta-AEs) compounds, analogs to E2, are possible candidates for use in hormone replacement therapy (HRT), but our knowledge of their pharmacological profile is limited. Thus, we explored the molecular recognition of GPER1 with different synthetic 17beta-AEs: prolame, butolame, and pentolame. We compared the structure and ligand recognition sites previously reported for a specific agonist (G1), antagonists (G15 and G36), and the natural ligand (E2). Then, the biological effects of 17beta-AEs were analyzed through cell viability and cell-cycle assays in two types of female cancer. In addition, the effect of 17beta-AEs on the phosphorylation of the oncoprotein c-fos was evaluated, because this molecule is modulated by GPER1. Molecular docking analysis showed that 17beta-AEs interacted with GPER1, suggesting that prolame joins GPER1 in a hydrophobic cavity, similarly to G1, G15, and E2. Prolame induced cell proliferation in breast (MCF-7) and cervical cancer (SIHA) cells; meanwhile, butolame and pentolame did not affect cell proliferation. Neither 17beta-AEs nor E2 changed the activation of c-fos in MCF-7 cells. Meanwhile, in SIHA cells, E2 and 17beta-AEs reduced c-fos phosphorylation. Thus, our data suggest that butolame and pentolame, but not prolame, could be used for HRT without presenting a potential risk of inducing breast- or cervical-cancer-cell proliferation. The novelty of this work lies in its study of compound analogs to E2 that may represent important therapeutic strategies for women in menopause, with non-significant effects on the cell viability of cancer cells. The research focused on the interactions of GPER1, a molecule recently associated with promoting and maintaining various neoplasms.
abstract_zh: 雌激素G蛋白偶联受体（GPER1）是一种跨膜受体，参与多种肿瘤的发生与发展，其配体为雌二醇（E2）。17β-氨基雌激素（17β-AEs）化合物作为E2的类似物，可能成为激素替代疗法（HRT）的候选药物，但对其药理学特征的了解仍有限。因此，我们探讨了GPER1与不同合成17β-AEs（prolame、butolame和pentolame）的分子识别机制。我们比较了先前报道的特异性激动剂（G1）、拮抗剂（G15和G36）及天然配体（E2）的结构和配体识别位点。随后，通过细胞活力和细胞周期实验，在两种女性癌症中分析了17β-AEs的生物学效应。此外，还评估了17β-AEs对癌蛋白c-fos磷酸化的影响，因为该分子受GPER1调控。分子对接分析显示，17β-AEs与GPER1相互作用，表明prolame以类似于G1、G15和E2的方式结合到GPER1的疏水腔中。Prolame在乳腺癌（MCF-7）和宫颈癌（SIHA）细胞中诱导细胞增殖；而butolame和pentolame不影响细胞增殖。在MCF-7细胞中，17β-AEs和E2均未改变c-fos的激活。与此同时，在SIHA细胞中，E2和17β-AEs降低了c-fos的磷酸化。因此，我们的数据表明，butolame和pentolame（而非prolame）可能用于HRT，且不会带来诱导乳腺癌或宫颈癌细胞增殖的潜在风险。本工作的新颖性在于研究E2类似物化合物，这些化合物可能为更年期女性提供重要的治疗策略，且对癌细胞活力无显著影响。研究聚焦于GPER1的相互作用，该分子近期被关联于促进和维持多种肿瘤。
